title: Miscellaneous Provisions under GST
outcomes: Apply provisions on information, evidence and burden of proof.
Apply saving of proceedings, rectification and rounding off.
Determine valid service of notices and compute time.
Explain special procedures and other enabling provisions.

meta.exam_tip: For service questions, identify the mode, its deemed date and whether the person acted on the notice.

concepts.title: Information, documents and evidence
body: Sections 144 and 145 presume documents produced or seized to be true and signed by the person named, and admit microfilms, facsimiles and computer printouts as evidence subject to conditions. Section 155 places the burden of proving ITC eligibility on the person claiming it.

Under section 151 the Commissioner may direct any person to furnish information on matters connected with the Act. Section 152 bars publishing such information in a way that identifies a person without written consent, or using it in proceedings without hearing the person; class-wise publication in public interest is allowed.
Section 158A permits consent-based sharing of registration, return, invoice and e-way bill particulars with notified systems. Section 154 allows officers to take samples against a receipt.
concepts.analogy: Evidence rules favour records; the claimant proves ITC.
concepts.work: A buyer claiming ITC must show invoice, receipt of goods and payment to supplier.

concepts.title: Saving of proceedings, rectification and rounding off
body: Section 160 keeps assessments, notices, summons, appeals and similar proceedings alive despite a mistake, defect or omission, if in substance they conform to the Act. Service of a notice cannot be questioned once the person has acted on it or has not objected at the earliest stage.

Under section 161 any authority may correct an error apparent on the face of record in its decision, order, notice or certificate, on its own, on an officer's pointing out, or on the affected person's request made within 3 months. The outer limit is 6 months from issue, except for purely clerical or arithmetical slips. A debatable point of law is outside its reach, and natural justice applies if the change is adverse.
Section 170 rounds tax, interest, penalty, fine, refund and other sums to the nearest rupee: fifty paise or more go up, less than fifty paise are dropped. Invoices themselves need no rounding.
concepts.analogy: Substance over form; errors fixable within limits.
concepts.work: A wrongly spelt name in a notice does not void the proceedings.

concepts.title: Service of notices and computation of time
body: Section 169 lists modes of serving notices: delivery to the person or an authorised representative, adult family member or employee; registered or speed post or courier with acknowledgement; e-mail given at registration; making it available on the common portal; newspaper publication; and, failing these, affixing at the last known place of business or on the office notice board.
Service is deemed on the date of tendering, publication or affixing. Communication by registered or speed post is deemed received at the end of the normal transit period unless proven otherwise.

Section 9 of the General Clauses Act, 1897: in counting periods, exclude the first day (the word "from") and include the last day (the word "to"). Section 172 lets the Government remove difficulties by order within 5 years of commencement.
concepts.analogy: Portal upload counts as valid service.
concepts.work: Thirty days from 1 June ends on 1 July.

concepts.title: Special procedures and other provisions
body: Section 148 allows special procedures for registration, returns, payment and administration for notified classes. Examples include exemption from tax on advances for goods and the corporate insolvency procedure, under which a corporate debtor under CIRP (where it has defaulted in GSTR-1 or returns) takes fresh registration as a distinct person within 30 days of the IRP/RP's appointment.

Section 149 provides for compliance ratings placed in the public domain. Section 156 treats officers as public servants; section 157 protects acts in good faith; section 162 bars civil courts, though appeals to High Courts and the Supreme Court remain.

Section 164 allows rules (with penalty up to ₹10,000 for breach), section 168 lets the Board issue instructions for uniformity, and section 17 of the IGST Act apportions IGST between the Centre and States.
concepts.analogy: Enabling provisions keep the system flexible and fair.
concepts.work: An IRP takes over GST compliance of a corporate debtor during insolvency.

jobs.title: Notice tracking
jobs.situation: Notices arrive on the portal, by e-mail and by post.
steps: Log date of service for each mode.
Compute reply deadline excluding the first day.
Seek rectification of obvious errors within 3 months.
jobs.takeaway: Missed portal notices still count as served.

viva.model: It keeps proceedings valid despite a mistake, defect or omission when they conform in substance to the Act.

viva.q: When can information under section 151 be published?
viva.model: Identifying publication needs written consent of the person; class-wise publication in public interest is permitted.

viva.q: What is a GST compliance rating?
viva.model: A rating under section 149 based on compliance record, revised periodically and placed in the public domain.

viva.q: Is a debatable legal point rectifiable under section 161?
viva.model: Rectification covers only errors apparent on the face of record; debatable points of law fall outside it.

viva.q: When is a speed-post notice deemed received?
viva.model: At the end of the normal transit period, unless the contrary is proved.
